Temporal memory

Present the current experience, then change it. The next state carries a trace of the last.

No experiences presented. Slider previews do not advance memory.

Subtract an ingredient

Paired interventions on the current experience, with model weights and memory frozen.

Remove memory, context, nonvisual senses, object shape, or emotion from both agents.

Let representations develop through learning.

Two small networks learn category reports, approach/avoid behavior, and reconstruction of their experiences. Their eight hidden units have no predefined subjective meaning.

Training protocol

700 experiences per agent. Both begin with the same weights; different histories change correlations in context, memory, texture, and emotion.

No trained model yet. The transparent model is active.

Compare coordinate systems

Fit a linear map from B's hidden states to A's on 192 calibration experiences. Evaluate on 192 separate experiences.

A smaller held-out error after alignment suggests some raw differences can be explained by a coordinate change.

This flexible ridge map can rescale and shear. It does not prove identical geometry, information, or experience. Slider and agent changes invalidate it.

What is actually learned?

16 inputs→8 tanh units→5 report heads + action

All hidden weights are trained. An auxiliary reconstruction objective encourages retention of experience beyond the reported category. Categories and behavioral targets are designer-chosen; no objective teaches or measures conscious experience.

Training will report accuracy on 300 fresh synthetic examples from a common evaluation distribution.

Same behavior. How different can the state be?

Search a seeded sample of experiences for matching report and action, then rank the matches by hidden-state distance. A match concerns only the outputs tested here.

Search protocol

Uses the active model, current modality, agent settings, and frozen sequence memories. Shared inputs vary across the full synthetic experience space.

No search run.

Best matching case

Train different histories or change Agent B, then search. Identical agents provide the zero-distance control.

Interpret the result carefully

The winner is the largest difference in this finite search, not a mathematical maximum. The test matches a category and a binary action; confidence, responses to future inputs, and other observables may still differ. A search result can demonstrate underdetermination in this model, never the existence of different qualia.

From a red apple to a general lab of experience.

The original conversation is preserved in the README and PDF, including the reasoning behind each iteration. The app is reconstructed from recovered descriptions because the original generated files were not available.

01 / EXPLORATION

Red apple, red ball

Separate a shared color signal from object identity, illumination, context, memory, emotion, and other senses. Establish identical and randomized controls.

02 / CAUSAL INTERVENTIONS

Two explicit agents

Follow stimulus → processing → context and memory → representation → report/action. Subtract ingredients and distinguish internal remapping from label changes.

03 / LEARNING

Learned internal states

Train eight-dimensional representations under identical, different, and inverted-label histories. Compare states before and after alignment.

04 / SEARCH

Behavioral twins

Search thousands of cases, carry temporal memory, and ablate a discovered case to explore what drives divergence.

Generalized edition

Vision, sound, touch, taste, and smell share one experiment engine. The modalities are abstract numeric channels, not calibrated physical stimuli or biological sensory models. Redness remains a reproducible starting case.

Working hypotheses

Identical deterministic systems should agree under identical complete state and input. Different histories can yield different representations with the same coarse behavior. Some differences disappear under coordinate alignment; others may persist under the tested mapping. Each is a testable statement about this model.

Scientific boundary

We do not infer consciousness from a vector, solve the inverted-spectrum problem, or equate a label with a feeling. Randomness adds variation, not subjectivity. A compensated hidden-unit inversion deliberately preserves the readout and is a control, not a discovery.

Next research direction · iteration 5

Compare representational geometry across many stimuli, add controlled coordinate-transform baselines, held-out behavioral batteries, repeated seeds, and uncertainty estimates. This roadmap is distinct from the completed iterations.

REAL TBP.MONTY · SYNTHETIC INPUTS

Learn an object by moving across it.

Run two Monty learning modules on the same feature-at-pose sequence. Change their training histories and inspect how evidence accumulates. Touch begins with simulated surface contact; each other modality has its own experimental adapter.

Sensorimotor experiment

Drive affects touch pressure and sound amplitude. It does not change vision, taste, or smell. A learns all three objects from 36 contacts each. Test contacts are shifted from the training locations.

Ready to run on the Mac mini. Nothing is precomputed or substituted for Monty.

One message format. Different sensors.

Modality-specific features+Location & orientation→Monty State→EvidenceGraphLM

Every adapter sends Monty's common feature-at-pose messages into the same graph-learning algorithm. Different feature definitions remain visible; common structure does not mean identical biological processing.

What “touch” means here

A scripted scan produces normalized pressure, roughness, and temperature features at known surface locations. No physical tactile sensor, skin model, haptic output, Habitat, or TACTO simulator is connected.

Sound, taste, and smell use supplied virtual locations and idealized poses. Those are experimental design choices, not claims that these senses naturally provide surface coordinates.

THEORY WORKBENCH / CLASSICAL & QUANTUM

Different mechanisms.
The same observable?

Explore phase memory in a simulated qubit and a classical oscillator. Ask what an experiment can distinguish before making a claim about consciousness.

A simulation of physics, not a consciousness detector.

One qubit, no entanglement, no physical quantum hardware. This is not Orch OR, a microtubule model, or a model of personal thought. Monty remains a separate sensory-learning experiment.

Design the comparison

All three models use the same delay, rotation and damping schedule. The stochastic control samples the oscillator's predicted probabilities. It is not a separately trained competitor.

Readout after a delay

━ Quantum prediction┄ Classical oscillator● Stochastic samples + 95% intervals┄ No phase memory

Generated locally from the displayed protocol. Intervals are pointwise Wilson intervals, not a simultaneous band. Each delay uses fresh preparations; the plot is not repeated measurement of one evolving qubit.

Outcome 0 probability
Normalized coherence
Quantum-state purity

What the mathematics actually says

Prepare |+⟩. At every step apply a Z-axis rotation by θ and a phase-damping channel that multiplies transverse Bloch components by (1 − d). A final Hadamard followed by a Z measurement yields P(0) = (1 + x)/2.

The classical control carries amplitude A and angle φ: A ← (1 − d)A; φ ← φ + θ. Its readout is (1 + A cos φ)/2. These models are analytically equivalent for this protocol. No parameter fitting is used. A 180° phase flip reverses x and y; erasure sets both to zero. Purity is (1 + x² + y²)/2; normalized coherence is √(x² + y²). Neither is a consciousness score.

The gray baseline erases phase memory immediately after preparation. It predicts ½ at every later delay. Arbitrary simulation steps are not mapped to neuronal timescales. This simple task tests phase retention, not task generalization, agency, selfhood, or quantum advantage.

RESEARCH MAP

Where does a physical mechanism meet a personal perspective?

01 / Physical substrate

Molecules, membranes, electrical activity, possible quantum mechanisms.

02 / Information processing

Representations, recurrent memory, prediction, shared access.

03 / Personal perspective

Body reference, learning history, self-attribution, goals, agency.

04 / Felt experience

The unresolved explanatory target. No curve above establishes its presence.

A thought's content, its format (imagery, language, abstract relations), and whether it is consciously experienced are different questions. Our working hypothesis is that ongoing thought involves evolving interactions among memory, perception, goals and action predictions. This remains a research framework, not a completed model.

Three claims. Three burdens of evidence.

Functional organization

Does a mechanism explain a defined capacity? Test retention, transfer, calibrated confidence, or agency attribution with controlled interventions. Performance alone does not settle phenomenal experience.

A quantum contribution

Identify a specific physical quantum state, show that it persists under relevant conditions, and demonstrate coupling to neural computation. Rule out ordinary biochemical explanations of the intervention.

Quantum necessity for experience

This stronger claim needs a bridge from a physical mechanism to experience, not just a behavioral benefit. Our simulation cannot establish it. An account must explain why its proposed process is necessary and what evidence would count against it.

Evidence, with its limits attached

PROPOSED NEXT EXPERIMENTS / NOT IMPLEMENTED

From phase memory to thought and selfhood

Compare a sensory baseline, recurrent memory, shared access across tasks, and self-prediction. These are experimental architectures, not levels of consciousness.

Present an object, remove it, introduce a new task, then perturb action feedback. Measure retention versus invention, transfer, agency attribution and confidence calibration. Selectively interrupt recurrence, inter-module communication or self-prediction. Match resources and training, include sham interventions, repeat seeds, and evaluate held-out situations.

Factors to separate: learned history, expectations, attention, goals, body-state variables, action feedback and temporal persistence. Changing a variable called hunger does not establish felt hunger. A selective loss of agency judgments with preserved recognition would be a functional dissociation, not proof of consciousness.
